subject: Private GPU pool: growth projection, autoscale & cross-VPC failover
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Casey Nguyen <casey@stellarhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private GPU pool: growth projection, autoscale & cross-VPC failover

Casey / Jordan,

Following up from last week's call — attached is an initial capacity projection and a proposed failover pattern for the private GPU pool we'll manage inside StellarHealth's VPC. High-level goals we took from the discovery:
- Production throughput target: sustained 180 requests/sec at average prompt+completion ≈ 1.2k tokens/request.
- P95 latency goal: <= 250ms for short-chat flows (~256 tokens) and <= 1.2s for long-form completions (~2k tokens).
- Allow for 3x peak burst for marketing/operational events.

Key assumptions encoded in the attached capacity_model_v2.xlsx:
- Model variant: quantized LlamaX-70B (8-bit) with mixed-precision kernel on A100-80GB equivalent.
- Effective tokens/sec per GPU (sustained, 2k context): ~9.5k toks/sec at steady-state with batching and KV reuse.
- Average concurrency per GPU for conversational mix: 14 concurrent sessions (based on 1.2k avg tokens).
- Network: each infer node requires ~18Gbps of egress headroom for aggregated token stream + control plane.

Proposal (short):
1) Initial pool: 12 GPUs (A100-80GB equiv) — covers steady 180 RPS with 1.5x headroom for small bursts.
2) Autoscaling: scale up to 36 GPUs in 5-minute increments based on token-queue-depth and 60s moving avg GPU util > 72%. Scale-down with conservative cooldown (10m) to avoid oscillation.
3) Burst/failover: pre-warm a cross-region burst pool (redwood-dedicated-burst) reachable via private interconnect/VPC peering. On saturation, route new requests to the burst pool using prioritized routing: primary (private pool) -> burst pool (same model, quantized) -> hosted fallback (redwood-hosted API) for non-sensitive traffic.
4) Caching: enable prefix cache for top-100 prompts and KV reuse for long contexts to reduce tokens/sec demand by estimated 18%.
5) Network & security: need a private peering link with min 40Gbps headroom and ability to failover DNS and route tables; KMS integration for keys when using cross-VPC resources.

Action items for StellarHealth to confirm:
- Expected peak-day QPS (marketing bursts) and scheduled events for the next 6 months.
- Any regulatory constraint that prevents cross-VPC inference (if so, fallback must be on-premises only).
- Preferred maintenance window for rolling upgrades and model swaps.

I've attached the capacity workbook and a simple failover/VPC diagram. Laura and Dev — please review the autoscale thresholds and the network assumptions and call out anything risky in this starting plan.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[attachment: capacity_model_v2.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Casey Nguyen <casey@stellarhealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Park <jordan.park@stellarhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private GPU pool: growth projection, autoscale & cross-VPC failover

Thanks Marcus — this is very helpful. A few quick clarifications from our side:
- Baseline traffic today is ~60 RPS, but we expect steady growth to 200-250 RPS over the next 9 months. We run two predictable daily peaks (09:30 and 15:00 PT) that last ~20-30 minutes.
- Regulatory: StellarHealth's data classification allows us to use cross-VPC compute if it stays within our approved cloud accounts and keys. We cannot send PHI to hosted public APIs.
- Maintenance window: Saturdays 02:00-05:00 PT is preferred.

Can you confirm the expected cost delta between starting with 12 GPUs vs starting with 18 (we're sensitive to committed spend but want to avoid frequent scale-ups)? Also, Jordan asked whether the burst pool warm-up time is dominated by model load (weights) or kernel warm-up.

Let's plan a 30-minute follow-up tomorrow to lock numbers.

—Casey
Casey Nguyen
VP Product, StellarHealth

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Casey Nguyen <casey@stellarhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 13:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private GPU pool: growth projection, autoscale & cross-VPC failover

Marcus — reviewing the workbook. Quick notes:
- The per-GPU tokens/sec estimate is conservative; if StellarHealth allows a lower precision path (int4 quantization for some completion classes) we can raise effective tokens/sec by ~30% which reduces GPU needs significantly. Call this the mixed-tier plan.
- Warm-up: model weight load is the main contributor (6–9 minutes for 70B on cold node), kernel JIT tends to be small if we're using prebuilt kernels in our runtime. Pre-warm strategy: keep a tiny warm pool (2 nodes) always hot during business hours and spin up new nodes using cached images to shave ~4–5 minutes off first inference.
- Autoscale: recommend two signals: token-queue-depth (primary) and 60s GPU util (secondary). For scale-down use a 15m sustained below-threshold check to avoid thrashing.

I'll attach a short commentary in the workbook and flag the scenarios where int4 is acceptable.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Solutions | Redwood Inference
[inline: see capacity_model_v2.xlsx sheet 'notes']

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Casey Nguyen <casey@stellarhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private GPU pool: growth projection, autoscale & cross-VPC failover

Casey — thanks for the data. To answer your two asks: cost delta and warm-up behavior.

Cost delta (very rough, non-accounting estimate included in workbook):
- Start at 12 GPUs (on-demand equivalent) — estimated monthly infra cost: $98k; operating with 1.5x headroom will likely hit autoscale events several times/month during growth windows.
- Start at 18 GPUs reserved — estimated monthly infra spend: $140k, but with lower risk of immediate scale events and smoother latency SLO adherence.
- If we use mixed-tier (int4 for non-sensitive bulk), modeled cost for hybrid pool compresses to ~$82k/month equivalent.

Warm-up: primary drag is model weight read-in + memory allocations. If we use cached AMIs/instance images and load weights from local NVMe (snapshot attached to instance), cold-start gets to first token in ~90s for a quantized 70B; unquantized might take 6+ minutes. Kernel JIT variability is modest if runtime uses precompiled kernels.

Recommendation: start 12 GPUs, enable a small reserved warm pool of 3 pre-warmed instances during business hours, and add policy to jump-to-18 GPUs when 5-min token-queue >= threshold. This balances cost and SLO risk. For PHI flows, ensure the fallback to hosted is blocked — only burst pool in approved accounts allowed.

Would you be available tomorrow 10:00 PT for a quick decision meeting? I'll have the cost slides and the autoscale YAML ready.

Marcus

From: Casey Nguyen <casey@stellarhealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Jordan Park <jordan.park@stellarhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 15:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private GPU pool: growth projection, autoscale & cross-VPC failover

Marcus / team — appreciate the clear options. We reviewed internally and want to proceed with:
- Start: 12 GPUs with a 3-node warm pool during business hours.
- Autoscale: policy you proposed (token-queue primary, 60s GPU util secondary; jump-to-18 when 5-min queue above threshold).
- Quantization: we'll onboard a mixed-tier plan — int4 for anonymized batch jobs, int8 for PHI-sensitive flows.
- Networking: we'll provision a redundant 100Gbps private link between our VPCs to Redwood's burst pool account; security will validate KMS cross-account access.

Confirming availability for the decision meeting 10:00 PT tomorrow. Please include a short runbook for incident response (how we fail traffic, how we test failover).

—Casey
